CPX-20045.name: AP5-Spastizin-spatacsin complex
properties:
The alpha-solenoid domain of ZFYVE26 binds in a parallel manner to SPG11's alpha-solenoid domain, forming a curved structure where the alpha-solenoids coil around each other throughut the core assembly forming tight dimeric contacts.

SPG11's WD40 N-terminal domain interacts with AP5 and is thought to play a key role in AP5 activation by stabilizing the AP5Z1 solenoid-solenoid interface and allowing for the open complex formation. Disrupting the SPG11-AP5 interaction results in the enlargement of the endolysosomal compartment.

CPX-5181.name: AP-5 Adaptor complex
properties:
Member of the adaptor protein (AP) complex family, which includes AP-1, AP-2, AP-3, AP-4 and AP-5 complex. 

All AP complexes are made of four different types of adaptin chains: one small sigma chain; one medium mu chain; and two large chains, a beta and gamma in AP-1, alpha in AP-2, delta in AP-3, epsilon in AP-4 and zeta in AP-5.

AP complexes also share similar structure, constituted of an 90 × 70 × 70 A globular core or head flanked by two approximately 30 A globular appendages or ears. The stalk or hinge that joins the head to the ears is thought to be flexible because the disposition of the ears with respect to the head can vary.
